new_scholarship.description: The ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship is an SMU-administered award for applicants who are citizens of ASEAN member countries other than Singapore, applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at Singapore Management University. SMU publishes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, plus an annual living allowance of S$5,800, an annual accommodation allowance of S$3,000 and a one-time computer allowance of S$1,750 on enrolment. The scholarship itself carries no bond, but because the tuition coverage is conditional on accepting the MOE Tuition Grant, every international recipient is placed under the Ministry of Education's 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Recipients must maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0, reviewed at the end of each academic term, and are liable to repay liquidated damages on breach.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Applicants who are citizens of Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste or Vietnam, who hold outstanding high school results, show strong leadership and co-curricular records, and are applying for a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Eligibility criteria published by SMU: citizens from ASEAN member countries (excluding Singapore citizens); have strong leadership qualities and potential; present good co-curricular activities records; possess outstanding high school results; be applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU. SMU lists the ASEAN member countries as Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam. Recipients must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0, reviewed at the end of each academic term, and may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, bursary or university loan without prior written approval from the University. Applicants with international qualifications must also satisfy SMU's general admission requirement of at least 12 years of formal education and submit one standardised test score.

new_scholarship.english_requirement: One standardised test score is required for applicants with international qualifications. SMU accepts any one of: SAT, ACT (American College Test), IELTS (Academic Test), TOEFL, C1 Advanced, Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic), or Aptitude Scholastic Test (AST). SMU states that both the TOEFL iBT and IELTS Online are acceptable for consideration of admission, and that SAT, ACT, IELTS, TOEFL, C1 Advanced, PTE Academic and AST are not required for applicants with an IB Diploma or acceptable diplomas from LASALLE College of the Arts, NAFA and NIE. new_scholarship.selection_notes: 'Scholarships are awarded based on merit and competition among eligible applicants.' 'Shortlisted candidates will be notified in due course.' The decision of the selection committee is final, and no appeals or disputes will be entertained.' SMU's Important Dates page states that only shortlisted applicants will be invited for scholarship or admissions interviews, and that interview notifications and application outcomes are sent in batches. No assessment weighting, quota, panel composition or tie-break rule is published.
new_scholarship.notes: SCOPE: the ASSIGNMENTS.md b132 row is 'SMU Undergraduate Scholarships for International Students', host smu.edu.sg, Singapore - the umbrella page https://admissions.smu.edu.sg/scholarships/prospective-students/international-students. That page lists three SMU-administered awards for international students (Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme, ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship, Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship) plus donor-funded awards. This record documents the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship because it is the SMU-administered international award on that page for which SMU publishes complete current figures (full subsidised tuition coverage after the MOE Tuition Grant, S$5,800 annual living allowance, S$3,000 annual accommodation allowance, S$1,750 one-time computer allowance), an explicit renewal CGPA, explicit bond wording and a complete terms-and-conditions section. The other two were seen only as index-page listings. DUPLICATION: EXISTING_AWARDS.json already contains 'SMU Merit Scholarship' (Singapore Citizens only, bond-free, full four-year tuition waiver plus S$12,000 growth opportunities allowance) and 'SMU Global Impact Scholarship Award', both on admissions.smu.edu.sg; neither is this award, and a scan of all existing award names found no ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship entry, so this is not a duplicate. Slot b130 is the NTU ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship on ntu.edu.sg, a different awarding body and a different award, so it does not collide. FUNDING: funding_amount is the S$5,800 annual living allowance, the only single recurring figure SMU publishes; the tuition element is a coverage statement, not an amount. BOND: the scholarship itself carries no bond, but the mandatory MOE Tuition Grant means every international recipient serves a 3-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, which forces fully_funded false. 75 PER CENT RULE: the widely stated Singapore scholarship condition that at least 75% of graduation credits be earned in Singapore was searched for and appears in NUS and NTU ASEAN scholarship terms, but is NOT published on SMU's ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship page; SMU instead publishes that overseas programmes of up to one academic term are allowed and not permitted in the final year. No 75% claim is asserted for SMU. LOGO: the dark header SVG was probed and confirmed to return real image bytes, contradicting the earlier audit note that this asset returned text/html. UNVERIFIED: AY2027-28 dates, numeric minimum standardised test scores, award quota, exact subsidised tuition fee amount, and liquidated damages figures.

programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The published benefit is '100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant - scholarship recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant)'. Two limitations keep fully_funded false. First, the coverage is of subsidised tuition fees only and is calculated after the MOE Tuition Grant, so any non-subsidised component and any compulsory ancillary, laboratory or miscellaneous fee is not stated to be covered. Second, and decisively, the coverage is conditional on accepting the MOE Tuition Grant, which for international students carries a 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately upon graduation; MOE confirms independently that 'Tuition Grant recipients who are Singapore Permanent Residents or international students must serve a 3-year bond after graduation.' An unavoidable service obligation means the record cannot be represented as fully funded.

award_holder_conditions: Must accept the Ministry of Education (MOE) Tuition Grant: 'While the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship carries no bond, recipients are required to accept the Ministry of Education (MOE) Tuition Grant.'

MOE Tuition Grant bond: 'Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who accept the Tuition Grant will be subject to a bond requiring them to work for a Singapore-registered company for a period of three (3) years immediately upon graduation.'

MOE confirms the bond independently: 'Tuition Grant recipients who are Singapore Permanent Residents or international students must serve a 3-year bond after graduation.' Only full-time employment after graduation counts towards the bond, and MOE describes the employer as a Singapore entity, which may be a company incorporated in Singapore or a foreign company with a substantial connection to Singapore.
Academic performance: 'Scholarship recipients must maintain a minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 3.0 out of 4.0. Academic performance will be reviewed at the end of each academic term.'

Overseas programme participation: 'Recipients may participate in overseas programmes lasting up to one academic term. Participation in such programmes is not permitted during the final year of study.'
Double Degree Programme coverage: 'The scholarship covers students enrolled in Double Degree Programmes, provided that both degrees are completed within the standard four-year student tenure.'
Withdrawal: 'The University reserves the right to withdraw the scholarship at any time if the recipient's academic progress or conduct is deemed unsatisfactory.'
Concurrent awards: 'Scholarship recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarships, bursaries, or university loans without prior written approval from the University.'

Post-graduation employment: 'Scholarship recipients are responsible for securing their own employment to fulfill the obligations of the MOE Tuition Grant bond. SMU does not guarantee or provide job placement upon graduation.'
Termination and repayment: 'In the event of premature termination of the scholarship or breach of any of the stated terms and conditions, the recipient shall be liable to repay liquidated damages.'
supplements_or_initiatives: Overseas programmes of up to one academic term, permitted except during the final year of study

programme_detail_official.description: The ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship is an SMU-administered undergraduate award from Singapore Management University for applicants who are citizens of ASEAN member countries other than Singapore and who are applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU. SMU publishes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, an annual living allowance of S$5,800, an annual accommodation allowance of S$3,000 and a one-time computer allowance of S$1,750 on enrolment. The scholarship carries no bond of its own, but because the tuition coverage is conditional on accepting the MOE Tuition Grant, every international recipient is placed under the Ministry of Education's 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Recipients must keep a cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 at the end of every academic term, may take at most one term of overseas programme outside the final year, and must repay liquidated damages if they breach the terms.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Subsidised undergraduate tuition fees in full after the MOE Tuition Grant, plus an annual living allowance of S$5,800, an annual accommodation allowance of S$3,000 and a one-time computer allowance of S$1,750. Overseas programmes are permitted for up to one academic term and excluded from the final year of study, but no airfare or travel funding is published.

alerts.trigger: Evaluating this award as full funding
alerts.message: SMU publishes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees but only after the MOE Tuition Grant, and that grant carries a 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, with only full-time employment counting. Price the bond into any comparison rather than reading this as cost-free study.

SMU publishes no separate scholarship closing date. The award follows the undergraduate admission timeline, whose published closing date for international and other qualifications was 19 March 2026, 11.59pm, Singapore Standard Time for the AY2026-27 intake. Next-cycle dates were not published when this record was verified on 2026-10-03, so treat the deadline as variable rather than fixed.

The published cycle ran from mid-November to mid-March, shortlisted applicants attend an interview or test between March and May, and outcomes are released in batches from May to July. An application submitted after the closing date cannot be considered for the scholarship.

alerts.trigger: Test score deadline trails the application deadline
alerts.message: For AY2026-27 the application closed on 19 March 2026 but the standardised test score was due by 31 March 2026. Missing the second date after applying is an easy, avoidable loss.

alerts.trigger: Checking for a 75 per cent credits rule
alerts.message: The condition that at least 75% of graduation credits be earned in Singapore appears in the ASEAN scholarship terms of other Singapore universities, but SMU's own page does not state it. SMU publishes only that overseas programmes of up to one term are allowed and not in the final year. Confirm the credits position with SMU before assuming either rule.
The scholarship still applies to Double Degree Programmes only if both degrees are completed within the standard four-year student tenure.

submission_workflow: 1. Confirm ASEAN citizenship other than Singapore citizenship and check your qualification against SMU's list of accepted international qualifications.
2. Sit one accepted standardised test if you do not already hold one, and register for the electronic score send.
3. Complete the SMU online application for admission for a full-time undergraduate degree programme.

4. In the Scholarship section of that application, indicate interest in the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship. There is no separate scholarship form, so an application that omits this is not considered.
5. Upload standardised test scores via Applicant's Self Service and submit the application before the published closing date, with the test score by its own later deadline.
6. Submit through the Applicant's Self Service Portal as the scholarship page requires.
7. If shortlisted, attend the interview or, for Law, the writing test.
8. If offered the scholarship and admission, accept the MOE Tuition Grant as part of the offer, since the tuition coverage depends on it.
9. On enrolment, keep the CGPA at or above 3.0 out of 4.0 in every academic term, avoid taking an overseas programme in the final year, and do not accept a concurrent award without written approval.

research_notes.logo: FOUND AND PROBED, but expect dedupe at merge time. Hunt order: the header and footer marks on https://admissions.smu.edu.sg/scholarships/prospective-students/international-students are file-backed, so I extracted the real asset URLs from the page's own img/link elements rather than guessing: site-headers/logo-smu-d.svg?revised=20251228 (the dark header wordmark), site-headers/logo-smu-t.svg (the light variant), and the favicon set. Probed live with a browser user agent and an image Accept header: logo-smu-d.svg returned HTTP 200, content-type image/svg+xml, and a decoded body of 39153 bytes beginning with an XML declaration and an Adobe Illustrator SVG export header, viewBox '0 0 131 70', with fill colours #141B4D, #1C1C4C and #8A704C - dark navy and gold, so it satisfies PART D rule 6 against white-on-transparent wordmarks. The PNG favicons were also confirmed as real image bytes by signature (favicon-32x32.png 722 bytes, favicon-16x16.png 395 bytes, apple-touch-icon.png 5626 bytes, all starting 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A, the PNG magic number), but they are low-resolution marks and the dark SVG is the proper wordmark. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE EARLIER AUDIT: research/bachelor/LOGO_AUDIT_REPORT.md lists admissions.smu.edu.sg as returning text/html, and that is true of the HTML pages themselves - a plain non-browser request to https://admissions.smu.edu.sg/financial-aid/international-students returned HTTP 200 text/html with a 212-byte Incapsula interstitial body - but it does not hold for these static asset paths, which served genuine image bytes on the same host. Because PART D keys entries by official source host and official_logo_overrides.json already has an admissions.smu.edu.sg entry pointing at this same SVG, this entry will most likely be deduped rather than added; note that b132's row host is smu.edu.sg while the served asset is on admissions.smu.edu.sg, and logo_host_taken is false only because the row host string differs from the existing override key. Official host is true because the bytes are served by SMU's own domain. The light variant logo-smu-t.svg was not used, since the dark variant is the one safe on a light card.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The official SMU page states the eligibility criterion 'Be applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU' and the benefit '100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees'. SMU's site structure places the award under Undergraduate > Be An SMU Scholar > Prospective Students > International Students, and the page's APPLY NOW link points at the undergraduate admission application.
research_notes.access_notes: admissions.smu.edu.sg sits behind an Incapsula WAF. Plain HTTP clients get a 212-byte text/html interstitial, so all SMU page text in this record was read through a real browser session. Static asset paths under /themes/smubase_5g/assets/ were reachable directly and were byte-verified. moe.gov.sg served normally to plain clients. Two MOE deep links (bond-matters detail and FAQ) returned the Tuition Grant Scheme hub page or HTTP 404, so the bond wording was taken from the hub page's own sentence plus the SMU page's fuller wording.
